RQ1.rationale: Directly presents a general CubeSat power-subsystem model using requirements, structure, behavior, and analysis packages, plus reusable assumptions/profile mechanisms. It also states limited behavioral scope and extension path.

RQ2.rationale: Claims reduced design time/cost, reproducibility, accessibility, traceability, and learning benefits, but provides only prototype scenario evidence and no reliability, integration-test, or quantitative outcome assessment.

RQ3.rationale: Directly integrates pre-physical requirement and parameter verification into the EPS model by extracting constraints from Papyrus .uml and generating respected/not-respected traceability outputs.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The authors explicitly position the work as an extension of the INCOSE SSWG CubeSat System Reference Model lineage; this extraction uses only the current Markdown and supplied metadata.

RQ1: The paper models a generic CubeSat EPS through requirements, structure, behavior, and analysis packages in Papyrus/SysML, using the CSRM lineage as a reusable starting point.
The behavioral burden is intentionally limited: use cases and one nominal sequence diagram are included, while AD/SMD and mission modes are excluded or left for extension.
Limited or externally fixed knowledge is handled through explicit assumptions that the Java workflow can identify and apply during power-budget analysis.
RQ2: Reproducibility is claimed through open-source Papyrus and repository publication; reuse is supported by the assumptions profile and proposed future standard component profiles.
Cost/time reduction, early error detection, learning, and rapid scenario evaluation are claimed, but only traceability/scenario evaluation has moderate case evidence.
Reliability is not measured directly; integrability is mainly represented as model/data integration and toolchain continuity rather than hardware or organizational integration evidence.
RQ3: Verification is integrated before physical development by encoding requirement constraints and power-budget equations in the SysML model and extracting them from the Papyrus .uml file.
The Java code evaluates user-changed parameters, applies assumptions, recalculates dependent values, and marks constraints as respected or not respected.
A worked EPS scenario demonstrates agreement between expected power-budget calculations and Java-generated outputs, but no physical integration or test campaign is reported.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Activity diagrams and state-machine diagrams were not used because they were not essential for the analysis.
